title: Efficient and Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Framework for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
claim: A two-phase system distills fast diffusion components offline, then adds uncertainty and shift awareness to guide online policy sampling.
layout: Two-phase, left-to-right, central module stack, cyan highlights marking the new components
description: The figure shows an offline-to-online RL framework in two phases. On the left, 'Offline Pre-training' in a red-bordered box shows a 3D stacked tensor of trajectory tokens (tau for states and actions) with a denoising arrow and a planning-horizon axis. An arrow labeled '1.2 Progressive Distillation' leads to a smaller matrix with cyan entries for the policy and transition. Cyan arrows labeled 'Policy & Transition Extraction' point to the center. The center has a Replay Buffer cylinder above a rounded box holding the Critic Model, Diffusion Policy Model and Diffusion Transition Model. On the right, 'Online Fine-tuning' has a robot, shown as policy pi_theta, interacting with an Earth icon for the environment dynamics. Below it, a box shows a Laplace-approximated posterior and a seen vs unseen shift histogram. Cyan text and arrows mark the new uncertainty components, and a 'Policy Sampling' arrow runs back to the robot.
caption: DUAL's overview framework, including an efficient diffusion actor policy & transition function extracted from diffusion planner, and a high-quality epistemic UQ & transition shift-awareness for policy sampling (colored by cyan). Overall algorithm is in Alg. [ref].
abstract: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning (O2O-RL) leverages an offline, pre-trained policy to minimize costly online interactions. Although data-efficient, O2O-RL is susceptible to shifts between offline and online distributions. Existing work aims to mitigate the harm of this shift by finetuning the policy on trajectory data sampled from a diffusion model. Inspired by this line of work, we propose DUAL: an efficient \textbf{D}iffusion \textbf{U}ncertainty-\textbf{A}ware framework for offline-to-online reinforcement \textbf{L}earning. DUAL utilizes the prior knowledge of the diffusion model to distill a fast-sampling diffusion actor policy and transition model in the offline phase. DUAL also employs a Laplace approximation and distance transition-state-shift detection, thereby using uncertainty quantification to improve exploration versus exploitation in the online phase. We formally show that our actor loss with the Laplace approximation provides a proxy for a principled estimate of epistemic uncertainty. Empirically, DUAL improves the online expected return over O2O-RL baselines across multiple settings and environments.
